issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to “Implement assembleBookstore which prints the Bookstore status (return type Void)”, which implies assembleBookstore should perform printing and return Void. However, the template provides (commented) a function signature that returns a Bookstore (private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore) and the solution implements assembleBookstore() to return a Bookstore while printing is done in Client.main(). This mismatch can confuse students about whether assembleBookstore should return the Bookstore or perform printing itself. If a student follows the problem text and implements assembleBookstore as Void (printing internally), automated tests or the provided template that expect a Bookstore return value (and the example solution) may fail.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the intended behavior explicit and consistent across artifacts. Preferably update the problem statement to state that assembleBookstore should return a Bookstore (e.g. "private static func assembleBookstore() -> Bookstore") and that Client.main() is responsible for printing the inventory. Alternatively, adjust the template and solution to have assembleBookstore return Void and perform printing inside it — but ensure tests and all artifacts are updated accordingly. The simplest fix is to remove "(return type Void)" from the problem statement and explicitly mention that assembleBookstore returns a Bookstore.
